prompt_text: What is the best AI video ad maker?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” — the right AI video ad maker depends on what you need (scale, creative control, budget, platform, whether you want AI avatars, etc.). Below are the top options in 2024 and when to pick each.

Top choices and when to use them
- Synthesia — Best for avatar-driven, multilingual, scalable ad personalization
  - Strengths: realistic AI presenters, many languages/voices, good for product explainers and localized ads at scale.
  - Weaknesses: less flexible for cinematic editing; enterprise pricing for high volume.

- HeyGen (formerly Movio) — Good Synthesia alternative for fast text-to-video avatars
  - Strengths: fast, lower-cost options, decent avatar selection.
  - Weaknesses: fewer advanced editing features.

- Pictory — Best for repurposing long-form content into short social ads
  - Strengths: automatic highlight extraction, captioning, stock media, quick social formats.
  - Weaknesses: limited fine-grain creative control.

- Canva (Video) — Best all-rounder for marketers who want templates + simple AI tools
  - Strengths: huge template library, brand kit, built-in stock, easy resizing for platforms.
  - Weaknesses: not as powerful for advanced generative video or avatar A/V.

- InVideo / Promo.com / Animoto — Best for template-driven fast ad creation
  - Strengths: ad-focused templates, captions, simple timeline editing.
  - Weaknesses: less advanced AI generation.

- Descript — Best if you want transcription-first editing, overdub voice, and simple workflow
  - Strengths: fast editing via text, AI voice clone (Overdub), great for talking-head ads and tutorials.
  - Weaknesses: not avatar-style text-to-video.

- Runway — Best for creative/experimental ads and generative visuals
  - Strengths: powerful generative tools, inpainting, text-to-video style effects.
  - Weaknesses: steeper learning curve; costs can rise for heavy generation.

- VidMob / Smartly.io / Celtra — Best for scale, performance-driven and agency-level ad production
  - Strengths: automation, creative analytics, A/B testing and integration with ad platforms.
  - Weaknesses: enterprise pricing and onboarding.

How to choose (quick checklist)
- Output type: avatar + spokesperson vs. template-based vs. cinematic visuals
- Volume: single ads vs. hundreds of localized variants
- Platform: TikTok/Instagram Reels vs. YouTube vs. display/social feeds (aspect ratios, lengths)
- Budget: free/low-cost tools (Canva, Pictory, InVideo) vs. enterprise (Synthesia, VidMob)
- Needed features: script generation, AI voiceovers, automatic captions, brand kit, A/B testing, API

Recommendations based on common needs
- Fast social ads with templates and brand kit: Canva Pro or InVideo
- Repurpose webinars/podcasts into short ads: Pictory or Descript
- Create personalized/localized video ads with on-screen presenters: Synthesia or HeyGen
- Experimental, high-end generative visuals: Runway
- Large-scale creative optimization and analytics: VidMob or Smartly.io

Want a tailored recommendation?
Tell me:
- Which platforms (TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, Facebook)?
- Your budget (free, <$50/mo, $50–300/mo, enterprise)?
- Volume (single ad, dozens, hundreds)?
- Style (live actor, AI avatar, text-and-images, cinematic)?

I’ll suggest the single best tool and a quick workflow for your exact need.
